primary_meaning: Bread most commonly symbolizes God-given life, provision, and spiritual nourishment, understood supremely in Christian teaching as Jesus Christ, the “bread of life.”
primary_basis: Exodus 16:4-15, 31-35 — manna as bread provided by God in the wilderness.
Deuteronomy 8:3 — bread contrasted with, yet used to illustrate, dependence on every word from God.
John 6:32-35, 48-58 — Jesus identifies himself as the true bread from heaven and the bread of life.
Matthew 26:26-29; Mark 14:22-25; Luke 22:19-20 — Jesus identifies the broken bread of the Last Supper with his body.
1 Corinthians 10:16-17; 11:23-29 — bread signifies participation in Christ’s body and the unity of believers.

alternatives.meaning: The sacramental body or real presence of Christ in the Eucharist. Traditions agree that Eucharistic bread signifies Christ’s body but differ materially over whether and how Christ is objectively present.
God’s word or revealed truth as nourishment for spiritual life.
Ordinary material provision and the necessities of daily life rather than a specifically christological symbol.
The fellowship and corporate unity of the church, represented by many believers sharing or forming one loaf.
Sacred fellowship with God or God’s covenantal presence, especially through the bread of the Presence and sacred meals.
Affliction, sorrow, wickedness, or dishonestly obtained sustenance, as in expressions such as “bread of tears,” “bread of wickedness,” or “bread of deceit.”

notes: There is broad consensus around bread as life-sustaining provision and spiritual nourishment from God, especially Christ as the bread of life. Bread is nevertheless context-dependent and does not have one exclusive symbolic referent. Eucharistic interpretations are especially prominent but remain divided over the nature of Christ’s presence.
